summary.text: Jasmine Clark is the Democratic nominee in Georgia's 13th District, an open seat. A microbiologist who teaches at Emory University's nursing school, she has represented Georgia House District 108 since 2019 after defeating a Republican incumbent in 2018. She is running for Congress on a platform her campaign describes as defending healthcare, science-based policy, and democratic institutions.

paragraphs.text: Clark was born in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1982, and Wikipedia lists a Bachelor of Science from the University of Tennessee.
Ballotpedia lists a bachelor's degree in biological sciences and a master's degree in microbiology and molecular genetics, and she earned a Ph.D. in microbiology from Emory University.

She works as a scientist and instructor at Emory University's Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, directed the 2017 March for Science in Atlanta, and has worked with the Georgia Alliance for Social Justice.

Clark won Georgia House District 108 on November 6, 2018, defeating incumbent Republican Clay Cox, and took office on January 14, 2019. Her campaign website says she flipped a long-held Republican seat.

She won re-election in 2020, 2022, and 2024, and her committee assignments in the 2025-2026 session include Banks and Banking, Budget and Fiscal Affairs Oversight, Health, Higher Education, and Interstate Cooperation.

Clark announced her candidacy for Congress in June 2025, initially challenging incumbent Rep. David Scott in the Democratic primary, and won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 56.1% of the vote.
According to Ballotpedia, she lived in Lilburn, Georgia, as of 2020.
